_doc: THE DECLARED HOME FOR THE MANAGER'S CONCURRENCY CAPS. `scripts/ops/manager_preflight.py`
reads its limits from HERE and from nowhere else -- it hardcodes no number.
WHY A FILE RATHER THAN A CONSTANT. A cap that lives in code is changed by editing code,
which means the operator's own words about it live somewhere else and drift. Every entry
below therefore carries the operator's wording VERBATIM plus the date, so the number and
its basis cannot separate. `field beats comment` applies to this file too: if the prose
anywhere disagrees with `limit`, `limit` is what the check enforces and the prose is the
thing to fix.
THE TWO CAPS ARE INDEPENDENT AND NEITHER IMPLIES THE OTHER. Several sessions may share
one artifact; one session may hold several. Counting one and calling it the other is the
conflation MI-64 already had to correct once.
AND NEITHER OF THEM IS THE WIP CEILING. The operating model's ceiling of 8 counts
`in_flight` WORK OBJECTS (docs/claude/work/objects/*.yaml) and is enforced in CI by
scripts/ci/check_wip_ceiling.py. That is a THIRD register with a THIRD population.
Lowering the object ceiling to match a session cap would fail CI on the in-flight phase
objects and block the build -- MI-64's own root_cause says exactly this. Do not merge
these three numbers.
A `contested` ENTRY IS NOT A DEFECT TO TIDY AWAY. When two sources give different limits,
the check does NOT pick one: it grades the count against BOTH bounds and returns
`unknown` only when the answer actually depends on which is right. Over every candidate
limit is still a definite FAIL; under every candidate limit is still a definite PASS. So
an unresolved contest costs nothing except in the narrow band where it genuinely matters,
and there it refuses instead of guessing.

sessions.counts: concurrent work sessions the manager has assigned and not yet closed out
sessions.population: rows in docs/claude/work/SESSIONS.json whose `state` is in the enforced set, intersected with a LIVE list_sessions observation. A registry row alone is a claim, not an observation; a live row alone is not attributable to the manager.

contested.text: I think we need to limit ourselves to 3 concuurent work sessions - 8 seems like too much for to handle reliably, so lets start small and scale up based on what we actually know is feasible
contested.note: The only operator wording carried VERBATIM in the repo as of 2026-09-02T13:30Z. Followed by: 'LEt all the opne sessions close, but don't spawn new ones until 1 of the 3 slots is open' -- i.e. a spawn gate, not a forced stand-down.

contested.source: PR #10799 (OPEN, unmerged at 2026-09-02T13:30Z) 'manager: caps are 4 sessions AND 4 artifacts, independently', and the MI-68 spawn brief which states it as the operator's position
contested.text: NOT RECORDED VERBATIM ANYWHERE THIS SESSION COULD READ. That is precisely why this entry is `contested` rather than authoritative.
contested.note: Probably the later refinement, and probably correct. `probably` is not a basis, and MI-65's lesson that same day was a session blocking work on a claim about live state it had not probed.

sessions.resolution: MERGE #10799 (or edit this file) and set `limit` to the agreed number, moving the losing entry into `superseded`. Until then the check refuses only in the band 4 <= count <= 4 -- outside it, the contest does not matter and the verdict is definite.

artifacts.population: open, NON-DRAFT pull requests, EXCLUDING those labelled/titled DO-NOT-MERGE and those on `automation/` branches. Decided by the operator 2026-09-02 (DEC-20260902-WHAT-IS-AN-ARTIFACT, option C).

operator_decision.text: let's go with your recommendation for c, and I understand this will bite the next manager, but that is, like you said, exactly the point, so that's fine
operator_decision.acceptance_criterion: THE OPERATOR EXPLICITLY ACCEPTED THAT THIS WILL BITE THE NEXT MANAGER. That is the acceptance criterion, not a caveat to soften. A cap nobody ever hits is a cap that is not doing anything.

⚠️_the_LIMIT_was_known_and_the_POPULATIO: ⚠️ THIS KEY'S NAME IS DELIBERATELY KEPT IN THE PAST TENSE RATHER THAN TIDIED AWAY. The
population WAS null and this cap SHIPPED REFUSING; that is the thing worth remembering
about it, and renaming the key would erase it.
⚠️ MEASURED AT THE MOMENT OF DECIDING: the count was 10 against a limit of 4, so the
system is OVER THE CAP ON DAY ONE. That is a MERGE BACKLOG, not a definition error, and
it must NEVER be used to argue for widening the definition. A population chosen to make
the number pass would make this cap measure nothing -- the fabricated-comfort failure
this whole effort exists to end.
Why C and not the others: a DRAFT pr is work in progress, not a thing competing for the
operator's attention; #10780 is explicitly [RECOVERED -- DO NOT MERGE] and #10398 is a
bot artifact open since 2026-08-29. C counts the things that actually need a decision.
The alternatives, on the record so nobody re-derives them (all 17 open PRs, 13:30Z):
17  all_open_prs
16  excluding_do_not_merge
15  excluding_do_not_merge_and_automation
11  open_non_draft
10  open_non_draft_excluding_both   <-- CHOSEN
EVERY ONE exceeded 4, so the choice decided HOW FAR over the cap we are, never WHETHER.
'in_flight work object' was considered and rejected as the population because it
UNDERCOUNTS: an artifact can be a doc, a workflow, or a running soak with no object.
artifacts.resolution: DECIDED 2026-09-02. `manager_preflight.py::check_artifact_cap` now ENFORCES it with no code change -- it reads `definition` and computes that population itself.

⚠️_enforced_session_states_is_a_LOWER_BO: It scopes the cap to rows the manager itself declared live. A session absent from
SESSIONS.json is invisible to this count -- and that register has been measured incomplete
TWICE (MI-15: 3 of 6 absent; 2026-09-02: 26 of 55 unregistered, 17 of them carrying the
manager's own id as parent). So a count over this register UNDER-counts exactly when it
This is why the check requires a LIVE observation and grades an interval rather than a
number: the registry supplies attribution, the live read supplies existence, and neither
alone can produce a trustworthy count. `ready` is unobtainable without looking, here for
the same reason it is in handoff_check.py.
